about: The review's disagreements with the checks, as eight issues ranked by consequence: four faults no check raises (counted from Claude's review of dev's 83 opened pages and the 31 known), then four false alarms the checks still raise today (each rejected call re-checked on today's code, 2026-11-07, and counted where it is still major). Built into a page by tools/review_issues.py; Alessandro's decisions land in the page's `issues` collection, one document per key.

issues.title: Words drawn in the same colour as their band
issues.what: The page prints “Estimated patient responsibility $2,965.78” in white on a black bar. Our render draws the bar black and the words black, so the patient's total cannot be read.
issues.checks: Nothing. Every word is in the HTML, so no check sees a problem.
issues.claude: A major fault: the reader loses the line.
issues.often: 11 pages: dark bars, header rows and buttons whose words vanish.
issues.proposes: A new check: every line the page prints readable must be drawn with enough contrast against what lies behind it. If not, major.

issues.title: Labels and their amounts pulled apart
issues.what: The page prints each label with its amount on one line. Our render draws the three labels, then the three amounts under them.
issues.checks: Nothing. Every word is there, in an order the checks accept.
issues.claude: A major fault: you cannot tell which amount belongs to which label.
issues.often: 8 pages: totals, price lists, rows joined by leaders.
issues.proposes: A new check: a label and its value printed on one line must be drawn on one line. If not, major.

issues.title: Text drawn on top of other text
issues.what: The receipt prints “Date: 01/10/2021”. Our render draws each label over its value, so the line reads “Dat01/10/2021”.
issues.checks: Nothing. The words are all there, in order.
issues.claude: A major fault: the lines cannot be read.
issues.often: 8 pages: labels over values, signature blocks, chips over chips.
issues.proposes: A new check: two words apart on the page must not overlap in the render. If they do, major.

issues.title: Two boxes side by side, drawn one under the other
issues.what: The page prints “Year to date” and “Time off” side by side. Our render stacks them, and draws Time off as loose lines.
issues.checks: Only the line it lost (“Vacation used 40 h”). No check sees side by side become stacked.
issues.claude: A major fault: the page's layout is lost.
issues.often: 14 pages: cards, header boxes, a list beside its picture.
issues.proposes: A new check: blocks printed side by side must be drawn side by side. If stacked, major.

issues.title: Alignment flagged where nothing moved
issues.what: “Compass Outfitters” is printed at the left, after its logo. Our render draws it at the left too. It wraps on two lines and loses the logo, but those are other faults.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”. The check measured the name against its whole box, and the logo before it made it look pushed to the right.
issues.claude: Not an alignment fault: the name sits where the page puts it.
issues.often: 22 majors still raised on 18 pages: a name after a logo, a clause beside its hanging number, a size inside a chip.
issues.proposes: Raise an alignment fault only when the line itself moves on the page, its left, centre and right edges all more than a few pixels from where it is printed.

issues.title: A size change nobody can see, called major
issues.what: “OFFICE USE” is 11 px on the page and 10.8 px in our render.
issues.checks: Major: “printed at the body's size, drawn smaller than the body”. The page's labels are 11 px and the render's 11.5 px, so 10.8 px falls just under them.
issues.claude: Not a fault: the difference cannot be seen.
issues.often: 12 type majors still raised on 11 pages, most of this kind.
issues.proposes: Raise a size fault only when the line's own size, printed against drawn, differs by more than 10%.

issues.title: A name printed twice, compared with the wrong copy
issues.what: “Camila Park” is printed twice: a script signature (1) and a bold printed name (2). Our render draws both the same way.
issues.checks: Two majors: “script printed, sans drawn” and “sans printed, script drawn”. It compared copy 1 on the page with copy 2 in the render.
issues.claude: Not a fault: each copy is drawn as printed.
issues.often: 36 majors still raised on 4 pages (c0008, c0424, c0345, the payslip).
issues.proposes: Where the same words are printed more than once, pair each copy with the nearest copy in the render, not the first one found.

issues.title: Three columns: the check counts a mix-up 15 times
issues.what: Sections 2, 3 and 4 are printed as three columns, and our render keeps three columns. But it draws item (a) of section 2 in section 3's column, and 4.4 at the bottom under section 2.
issues.checks: 15 majors, one for every pair of sections: “their words alternate in the reading order”.
issues.claude: The 15 are one fault counted 15 times. The real faults are the two items drawn in the wrong column. Claude's first call named only 4.4; on a second look, (a) is out of place too.
issues.often: 20 majors still raised on 4 pages (c0221, c0374, c0384, c0464).
issues.proposes: Where the page sets columns, read the order column by column, and report only the items drawn in another column: here 2 faults, “under another heading”.
